chapter_note: Chapter is largely dominated by systematic cosmological/anthropological teaching: (a) how Sin/Matter retained the seal of the Ambassador’s image through its descent and generative transmission, and (b) a long correspondential microcosm-teaching of the senses as ‘storehouses’ with guards at bodily gates, culminating in Light Mind/Living Spirit taking control from Sin. Strong late drift appears at the end: a clear exhortation paragraph, and an ecclesial-sounding ‘psalms/prayers/hymns/charity’ paragraph that applies the sensory doctrine to community practice. Several paragraphs are MIXED only because of dialogue-attribution formulas (‘the enlightener says/speaks’), which are stripped from the extracted core_text.

paragraphs.core_text: All [these a]bortions, amongst them are Saklas and his consort and the ones whom they have served [ ... ], they are the ones that shaped Adam and Eve. How did they find this beautiful image laid over their shape, even though when it was displayed to their fathers they were not in existence? They never saw the image of the Ambassador! And how did they take the seal of the image of the Ambassador? They added it to [the] shape of Adam and Eve.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: "[Once again the] disciples questioned the enlightener. They say to him:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question (Saklas/Adam-Eve/Image of the Ambassador) is internal to the mythic system; the surrounding Q&A attribution is later compilation frame.

paragraphs.core_text: The enlightener [speak]s to them thus: The Sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [ ... / ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal causal chain (Sin/Matter → image → descent → tree/fruit → abortions) in impersonal explanatory voice; no citation or institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: [... in the] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [ ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological narrative remains within the rulers’ world (light used as substance for constructing an image).

paragraphs.core_text: Again the enlightener says: The Sin that s[purted out ... / ... ] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits ... ]. It went in to the rulers [ ... ] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the Sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted ... they] begat each of them according to his destiny [ ... ]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Repetitive, mechanical transmission-explanation (Sin/Matter as carrier of ‘seal’) characteristic of older teaching style; stays cosmos→cosmos.
Direct-address closure (“Behold, I have taught you…”) functions as didactic/applicative wrapping rather than impersonal substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is systematic microcosm teaching (limbs/senses as ‘storehouses’); only the speech-introduction is compilation frame.

paragraphs.core_text: In this way his faculty [ ... ] outer [limbs] to look at [ ... ] every type with [in ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary continuation of the same correspondential ‘faculty/limbs’ exposition; no editorial address.

paragraphs.core_text: Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [ ... ] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[st ... or a]n image of love [or ... / ... something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly systematic faculty-mechanics; ‘storehouses/repositories’ schema is classic Manichaean microcosm teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [ ... ] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, procedural description of sensory retention/retrieval; no institutional or Gospel overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: [In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [ ... ] and [ ... ] storehouse and remember [ ... ] only these things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the same systematic sensory schema.

paragraphs.core_text: However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [ ... ] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic ‘faculty + repository’ mechanics; correspondential focus (taste/mark/memory) stays within the anthropological microcosm model.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the five-sense ‘storage’ set in a uniform technical register.

paragraphs.core_text: And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Hierarchical governance teaching (heart ruling five faculties) in impersonal explanatory mode.

paragraphs.core_text: For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure simile used for structural correspondence (heart ↔ king/government) without contemporary institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [ ... / ... / ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second simile (cellarman/storage) continues the same ‘repository’ doctrine; internal pedagogic imagery.

paragraphs.core_text: ... in the place that it put it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragment closing the cellarman simile; no layer markers.

paragraphs.core_text: This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the technical ‘faculty/storehouse’ mechanism (body as integrator).

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Repetitive procedural language typical of the underlying teaching register.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds ... / ... ] they shall bring it out in to [ ... / ... ] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic completion of the sensory set; no editorial present-time anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core image introduces the ‘gates/guards’ correspondential model; attribution is later frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [ ... / ... ] that [ ... ] there are a mass [ ... / ... ] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [ ... ] are [ ... ] Whenever someone will wish [ ... ] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended structural simile (camp/gates/foreigners) serving the body-sense doctrine; despite mild ‘you shall find’ rhetoric, it remains explanatory rather than institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: "The enlightener says:"
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear microcosm mapping (camp→body; gates→orifices; guards→powers; ruling faculty→queen). Attribution is a later dialogue wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-soteriological mechanics (Light Mind vs rulers/guards) expressed as process; stays within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of Lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the Sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still mostly internal: Light Mind ‘takes bolts’ and reverses openings from Lust/Sin; some ‘practice of life’s concerns’ edges toward application but remains generic and embedded in the mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: So, now, bec[ause] the b[olt]s to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light M[in]d within, he is open [to receive] in all that is pleasing to God. He is op[en to take] in by his eyes the visions of lov[e ... ] and righteousness. Yet, now, by the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled Lust, the goddess of the body. The parades of Lust have become loathsome in the presence of the righteous person. How-ever, the aspects of divinity and righteousness and humility and scorned clothes are pleasing to him.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the illustrative excursion identifying lust-objects in contemporary social display: "Indeed, due to this, the si[ghts and] the [ad]ornme[nt of the gar]ments of kings... woven with gold and pearls... first they were lovable before the eyes of the chosen person." This portion crosses from cosmic mechanism to worldly exempla.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mechanism (Light Mind controlling bolts; Lust/Sin subdued) is substrate-like; the excised segment points outward to concrete elite clothing as temptation, suggesting later applicative expansion.

Entire paragraph applies the sensory doctrine to communal religious practice (psalms, prayers, hymns, charity) and moral instruction; this is cosmos→community ‘pointing at’ rather than system-internal exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: [S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief doctrinal summary in cosmic-agent terms (Sin ruling the body); rhetorical ‘at one time/now’ but not institutionally anchored.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Holly Spir[it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal cosmological agents (Living Spirit, Light Mind, Sin) governing the microcosm; ‘Holy Spirit’ appears as an internalized reign-title here without NT citation formula, so treated as part of the doctrinal system rather than Gospel-overlay.

Direct exhortation with audience address (‘my brothers…’), imperatives (‘make yourselves secure… be watchful…’), and practical guarding instruction: late applicative layer consistent with chapter-end editorial fatigue.
